    Dust monitor

      Dust along the route

      How to read the labels . OBSERVED: retrieved from an orbiter instrument for that cell and those sols. HISTORICAL: statistics of observations from other Martian Years. INTERPOLATED: estimated between observations (kriging), shown only when asked for. MODELLED: no dust value here is a model output. This is detection from past observations and a historical record, not a forecast. Optical depth describes the whole air column from orbit; it does not measure visibility or conditions on the ground.

        Imagery and layers: NASA/JPL Mars Trek (MRO HiRISE and CTX, Viking, Odyssey THEMIS, MGS TES and MOLA, Mars Express HRSC). Route, weather and rover photos: NASA/JPL-Caltech Curiosity (MSL, REMS, Navcam). Radiation is a model built on the published RAD surface average. Dust optical depth: Montabone et al. climatology (MGS TES, Odyssey THEMIS, MRO MCS), CC BY-SA 3.0.

        Settings

        Changes apply straight away and are kept for your next visit.

        Display

        Tick the readouts you want to see beside the map.

        How the readouts look

        Units
        Layout

        US units: feet, °F, psi and millirem. The column sits beside the map on wide screens; on narrow screens the readouts always run along the bottom.

        App colours

        The night themes are easier on the eyes in the dark; Night red keeps them adjusted to it. High contrast is for bright light.

        Walker

        Every recorded trail carries its walker's name and kind, and landmark visits are counted per walker.

        Trail

        Pointer

        Moving the pointer

        Keys are W A S D, the arrow keys and the on-screen pad. A tap walks the pointer to the spot you touch.
